newsitem.title: PERU: Peru government and rebels to meet again.
newsitem.headline: Peru government and rebels to meet again.

text.p: The Peruvian government and Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages in Lima were set to meet again on Thursday afternoon for a fourth round of face-to-face talks, government sources said.

Red Cross chief representative Michel Minnig and Canadian ambassador Anthony Vincent, who are overseeing the talks, arrived at the site of the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence shortly before 3 p.m. (2000 GMT).
Sources close to government negotiator Domingo Palermo told Reuters that he was scheduled to meet Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebnels in the afternoon.
Palermo met MRTA deputy leader Rolly Rojas last week in three rounds of talks that apparently brought nothing other than a commitment to meet again.

MRTA rebels took over the Japanese residence on Dec. 17, taking about 500 hostgaes. After a series of releases, they are holding the 72 remaining hostages as bargaining chips to press for the release of some 400 jailed comrades. President Alberto Fujimori's government has flatly ruled out freeing jailed rebels.
